title: 1981 AHSME Problem 11
statement: The three sides of a right triangle have integral lengths which form an arithmetic progression. One of the sides could have length

solutions.text:
If the sides are \(s-d,\) \(s,\) \(s+d,\) the Pythagorean equation gives \((s-d)^2+s^2=(s+d)^2,\) hence \(s=4k\) and \(d=k\) for some positive integer \(k.\) Thus the sides are \(3k,\) \(4k,\) \(5k.\) Of the choices, \(81=3\cdot27\) can occur.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Represent the three equally spaced sides as \(s-d,\) \(s,\) \(s+d\)
Every such integral right triangle is a multiple of a \(3\)-\(4\)-\(5\) triangle
